data.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 31 at 3:35AM EDT until November 2 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
data.description:
* WHAT...Moderate coastal flooding expected during periods of high
tide. Dangerous beach conditions with a high rip current risk.

* WHERE...Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 PM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
data.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

FXUS62 KMFL 311129
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
729 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 724 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

  - Moderate coastal flooding remains possible through at least
    Sunday. Inundated roadways along coastal areas will be
    possible during times of high tide.

  - Dangerous marine and beach conditions are expected across the
    Atlantic coast.

  - Slight Risk (level 2/4) for heavy rain leading to isolated
    flash flooding Sunday afternoon through Monday morning.

&&

.SYNOPSIS...
Issued at 322 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Deep layer ridging covers the Southeast and much of the center of 
the country, with a shortwave over eastern TX and the Lower MS 
Valley. Ensembles generally bring the shortwave through the 
Southeast overnight tonight through Monday morning, and only 
gradually nudge the low-level ridge axis northeastward. Then, 
ridging briefly builds back over the Southeast before a stronger 
frontal system reaches and crosses through the Southeast mid to late 
week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Sunday Night)
Issued at 322 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

The continued strong easterly flow at the base of the low-level 
ridge will keep the coastal trough in place and allow for scattered 
showers to move inland today and tonight. While the probability of 
rainfall across south Florida is high, the scattered nature of the 
showers makes it difficult to pinpoint where and when a location may 
be impacted by a passing shower. The one thing hi-res guidance does 
agree on is that the highest probability of heavier rainfall is in 
the late night/early morning hours (within training bands) with 
mostly light to moderate showers during the daytime. Additionally, 
with the exception of any training, showers should be rather brief 
since the steady easterly flow is expected to keep showers moving 
quickly.

The deep-layer forcing associated with the approaching shortwave is 
forecast to arrive late Sunday afternoon into the overnight hours. 
The primary expectation is more widespread rainfall with the assist 
from the large-scale ascent and high PWATs. With the low-level 
easterly flow expected to continue (and the associated trough 
remaining in place), the pattern of west-east oriented bands of 
heavier precip will likely continue but be enhanced by the support 
aloft. For these reasons the WPC has outlooked much of the Florida 
east coast with a Slight Risk for excessive rainfall on Sunday. 
Essentially this is a level 2/4 risk for isolated to scattered flash 
flooding potential. On average across South Florida, a reasonable 
worst case QPF would be on the order of 1.5-2", but wherever an W/E 
oriented band sets up, the reasonable worst case jumps closer to 3-
5". With those amounts likely to fall over the course of 1-3 hours, 
there would be a slight flash flooding risk. Since this risk runs 
through the overnight hours Sunday, into early Monday morning, WPC 
keeps the FL east coast under a Slight Risk in Monday's outlook as 
well.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Monday through Friday) 
Issued at 322 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

For the first part of next week we return to a pattern consisting of 
ridging aloft and moderate easterly flow around the base of a low-
level ridge. That means a return to scattered passing showers each 
day and night. The pattern will change a bit come mid-week when flow 
begins to veer ahead of a developing/approaching frontal system. 
There's still quite a bit of uncertainty around the pre-frontal 
environment and how mesoscale features will affect storm 
distribution each day, but guidance is in fair agreement of a 
frontal passage some time on Friday. How strong and how far south 
the surface low will be, and what that means for the potential for 
an isolated severe storm or two, remains in question with quite a 
bit of model spread. Certainly something to keep an eye on once we 
get past this weekends heavy rain threat.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 724 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

A lower cloud deck will bring MVFR ceilings to the region through
15z before gradually lifting to VFR across most of the terminals.
ENE winds will generally range between 10 to 15 kts with gusts of
20 to 25 kts possible throughout the day and into the evening
hours. Scattered showers will remain possible throughout the
forecast period and could bring periods of MVFR if they pass over
the terminals. 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 322 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Winds across the local Atlantic waters will increase through 
the morning, with gusts reaching the 20-25 kt range, while seas will 
build up to 7-10 ft (by late tonight) along the Gulf stream. 
Conditions across the Gulf will remain below hazardous criteria, but 
will need to be monitored closely. These impacts could last through 
the rest of the weekend as the stout pressure gradient and breezy 
easterly northeasterly winds prevail. Isolated showers remain 
possible today, with more widespread rain chances late this weekend. 

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 322 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Persistent and strong onshore flow will keep a high risk of rip
currents in place for the foreseeable future. Additionally, the
strengthening winds and building seas will result in surf heights
reaching advisory levels by this afternoon along Palm Beach and
Broward beaches.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Issued at 322 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Though we're on the back side of the King Tide peak, water levels 
are struggling to fall below moderate stage during high tide cycles 
due to the persistent, and at times strong, onshore flow. There may 
be a brief window where we're able to fall below moderate flood 
stage late Sunday through Monday, but once the easterly flow becomes 
established again early next week, guidance indicates the potential 
to flirt with moderate flood stage once again. We certainly won't be 
dealing with the levels seen during the peak of the King Tides, but 
a prolonged period of at least minor impacts at high tide should be 
expected through much of next week.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
Miami            84  76  82  74 /  60  60  90  80 
West Kendall     86  76  84  74 /  60  50  90  80 
Opa-Locka        85  75  83  73 /  50  60  80  80 
Homestead        86  76  84  74 /  60  60  90  80 
Fort Lauderdale  83  75  81  73 /  50  70  90  90 
N Ft Lauderdale  84  75  82  73 /  50  70  90  90 
Pembroke Pines   85  75  84  73 /  50  60  90  80 
West Palm Beach  84  75  82  72 /  40  50  70  80 
Boca Raton       83  75  82  73 /  50  60  80  90 
Naples           86  73  84  71 /  50  20  80  60 

&&

.MFL WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...Coastal Flood Advisory until 7 PM EDT Sunday for FLZ168-172-173.

     High Rip Current Risk through Monday morning for FLZ168-172-173.

     High Surf Advisory from 2 PM this afternoon to 7 AM EDT Monday 
     for FLZ168-172.

AM...Small Craft Advisory until 7 AM EDT Monday for AMZ650-651-670-
     671.

GM...None.
&&

$$
